job.title: WHS Advisor
job.description:
WHS On‑Site Advisor (Casual / Part‑Time)

Processing Plant / Industrial Operations

We are seeking a technically strong WHS On‑Site Advisor to support safety performance across our processing‑plant operations. This role suits an experienced safety professional seeking casual or part‑time hours while maintaining hands‑on involvement in high‑risk industrial environments.

About the Role

Reporting to the Production Manager, you will provide technical WHS support across daily operations, ensuring compliance with Australian WHS legislation and site‑specific risk controls. Responsibilities include:
  • Conducting formal site inspections, hazard identification and risk assessments
  • Leading and reviewing JHAs, SWMS and task‑based risk documentation
  • Monitoring critical controls in a processing‑plant environment (isolation, guarding, confined space, hazardous chemicals, mobile plant)
  • Supporting incident reporting, root‑cause investigations and corrective action verification
  • Delivering toolbox talks, pre‑starts and targeted safety coaching
  • Ensuring compliance with Australian WHS legislation, Codes of Practice and internal standards
  • Assisting with contractor management and verification of competency
Required Skills & Experience

To be considered, you must demonstrate:
  • Minimum Australian WHS qualification (e.g. Cert IV in WHS or higher)
  • Proven experience working in a processing plant, manufacturing, mining or heavy‑industry environment
  • Strong understanding of high‑risk work controls (LOTO, confined space, working at heights, hazardous substances)
  • Ability to interpret legislation, standards and technical safety documentation
  • Confident communication with operators, supervisors and management
  • Ability to work autonomously and provide practical, evidence‑based safety advice
What's on Offer
  • Casual or part‑time hours to suit your availability
  • Competitive hourly rate based on qualifications and experience
  • Opportunity to influence safety performance in a complex industrial environment
  • Supportive team with strong commitment to WHS excellence
How to Apply

If you are a technically capable WHS professional with hands‑on experience in processing‑plant operations, please submit your resume and availability for consideration.

  • Inspect, clean, lubricate and adjust mechanical components to maintain optimal performance.
  • Diagnose mechanical faults and identify the root cause of equipment failures.
  • Carry out mechanical repairs, component replacement and equipment servicing.
  • Respond to breakdowns and emergency maintenance requirements to minimise downtime.
  • Undertake basic welding, fabrication and machining as required.

  • Follow established marine industry procedures, workplace health and safety requirements and maintenance standards.
  • Identify and report potential hazards, equipment defects and safety issues.
  • Assist with continuous improvement initiatives to improve equipment reliability and reduce downtime.
  • Support and mentor junior maintenance personnel where required.
  • Maintain a clean, organised and safe workshop and work environment.
  • Ensure tools and equipment are returned to their designated locations at the completion of each shift.
You will be a practical and mechanically minded tradesperson with strong fault-finding skills and the ability to work independently while contributing to a broader maintenance team.

Ideally, you will have:
  • Certificate III in Engineering – Mechanical Trade, Mechanical Fitting or equivalent experience.
  • Proven experience in a mechanical maintenance role, preferably within marine, construction, manufacturing, heavy industry or a similar environment.
  • Experience working with marine structures, pontoons, jetties or related equipment will be highly regarded.
  • Basic welding and fabrication capabilities.
  • Strong mechanical troubleshooting and diagnostic skills.
  • Ability to read and interpret technical manuals, drawings and specifications.
  • Strong understanding of preventative and reactive maintenance practices.
  • High level of attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
  • Strong safety awareness and understanding of workplace safety procedures.
  • Ability to undertake physically demanding work and operate effectively in heat, rain and varied outdoor conditions.
  • Good communication and teamwork skills.
  • A proactive approach to identifying problems and finding practical solutions.

  • Variety of mechanical maintenance and repair work

  • Opportunity to develop your skills across mechanical, fabrication and marine equipment
